name: p27-text-0001
text: Manufacture of Mark VIII Tanks

name: p27-text-0002
text: at Rock Island Arsenal

name: p27-text-0003
text: By

name: p27-text-0004
text: HARRY B. JORDAN

name: p27-text-0005
text: Charter Member A. O. A.

name: p27-text-0006
text: E

name: p27-text-0007
text: Col. Harry B. Jordan

name: p27-text-0008
text: Commanding Officer Rock Island Arsenal

name: p27-text-0010
text: Colonel H. B. JORDAN,

name: p27-text-0011
text: Rock Island Arsenal,

name: p27-text-0012
text: Rock Island, Ill.

name: p27-text-0013
text: Dear Jordan:

name: p27-text-0014
text: I have just received your telegram concerning

name: p27-text-0015
text: the completion of the assembly of one hundred Mark VIII tanks

name: p27-text-0016
text: on the 10th inst. and I congratulate you on the successful termi-

name: p27-text-0017
text: nation of this order.

name: p27-text-0018
text: Sincerely yours,

name: p27-text-0019
text: [Signed]

name: p27-text-0020
text: C. C. WILLIAMS,

name: p27-text-0021
text: Major General, Chief of Ordnance, U. S. A.

name: p27-text-0023
text: ARLY in the Spring of 1919 there was received

name: p27-text-0024
text: at Rock Island Arsenal one of the largest orders

name: p27-text-0025
text: in its history. This order covered the assembly

name: p27-text-0026
text: of 100 Mark VIII Tanks.

name: p27-text-0027
text: The Mark VIII Tank

name: p27-text-0028
text: is a fighting tank, weigh-

name: p27-text-0029
text: ing about 40 tons when

name: p27-text-0030
text: fully equipped and man-

name: p27-text-0031
text: ned. It carries a com-

name: p27-text-0032
text: plement of 8 men, 1 in

name: p27-text-0033
text: the engine room and 7

name: p27-text-0034
text: in the fighting compart-

name: p27-text-0035
text: ment. The 7 men con-

name: p27-text-0036
text: sist of the officer in com-

name: p27-text-0037
text: mand, the driver, and 5

name: p27-text-0038
text: gunners; 2 of the gun-

name: p27-text-0039
text: ners manning the 6-pdr.

name: p27-text-0040
text: Hotchkiss guns and 3

name: p27-text-0041
text: the Browning machine

name: p27-text-0042
text: guns. The tank is equip-

name: p27-text-0043
text: ped with 2 Hotchkiss 6-

name: p27-text-0044
text: pdr. guns and 5 Brown-

name: p27-text-0045
text: ing machine guns and

name: p27-text-0046
text: provides storage for 200

name: p27-text-0047
text: rounds of 6-pdr. ammu-

name: p27-text-0048
text: nition and 20,000 rounds

name: p27-text-0049
text: of 30 cal. ammunition.

name: p27-text-0050
text: The platforms for the 6-

name: p27-text-0051
text: pdr. gun mounts are in

name: p27-text-0052
text: sponsons, one of which

name: p27-text-0053
text: is located on each side

name: p27-text-0054
text: of the tank, pivoting on

name: p27-text-0055
text: a vertical hinge partially

name: p27-text-0056
text: into the interior of the

name: p27-text-0057
text: tank when required, to

name: p27-text-0058
text: reduce the overall width.

name: p27-text-0059
text: The motive power is a

name: p27-text-0060
text: 12-cylinder Liberty mo-

name: p27-text-0061
text: tor developing approxi-

name: p27-text-0062
text: mately 400 hp. at 1400

name: p27-text-0063
text: r. p. m. The epicyclic

name: p27-text-0064
text: transmission provides for

name: p27-text-0065
text: two speeds forward and

name: p27-text-0066
text: one speed reverse. In

name: p27-text-0067
text: low gear, with the engine at 1400 r. p. m., the for-

name: p27-text-0068
text: ward speed is 1.4 miles per hour; in high gear, 5.2

name: p27-text-0069
text: miles per hour. The gasoline supply of 150 gallons

name: p27-text-0070
text: allows for ample cruis-

name: p27-text-0071
text: ing range. The cater-

name: p27-text-0072
text: pillar feature in the

name: p27-text-0073
text: tank is so designed that

name: p27-text-0074
text: no part of the tank ex-

name: p27-text-0075
text: tends to the front or to

name: p27-text-0076
text: the rear beyond the

name: p27-text-0077
text: treads, making it almost

name: p27-text-0078
text: nonstallable.

name: p27-text-0079
text: The hull, which is con-

name: p27-text-0080
text: structed of armor plate,

name: p27-text-0081
text: angle iron, steel chan-

name: p27-text-0082
text: nels, etc., provides the

name: p27-text-0083
text: framework for carrying

name: p27-text-0084
text: the engine, transmission,

name: p27-text-0085
text: fighting equipment and

name: p27-text-0086
text: accessories.

name: p27-text-0087
text: There were no build-

name: p27-text-0088
text: ings at Rock Island Ar-

name: p27-text-0089
text: senal specially adapted

name: p27-text-0090
text: for the assembly of the

name: p27-text-0091
text: Mark VIII tanks on a

name: p27-text-0092
text: production basis. The

name: p27-text-0093
text: craneway of Shop M (a

name: p27-text-0094
text: clear assembly space ap-

name: p27-text-0095
text: proximately 60 by 500

name: p27-text-0096
text: feet) equipped with two

name: p27-text-0097
text: 15-ton cranes, provided

name: p27-text-0098
text: the best space for the

name: p27-text-0099
text: hull assembly. In this

name: p27-text-0100
text: space it was possible to

name: p27-text-0101
text: work on approximately

name: p27-text-0102
text: 30 tanks at one time.

name: p27-text-0103
text: Each tank occupies a

name: p27-text-0104
text: floor space of approxi-

name: p27-text-0105
text: mately 410 square feet;

name: p27-text-0106
text: i. e., length 34 ft., width

name: p27-text-0107
text: 12 ft. While the as-

name: p27-text-0108
text: sembly space in the

name: p27-text-0109
text: craneway of Shop M

name: p27-text-0110
text: was less than should

name: p28-text-0112
text: have been available, still the building offered excellent

name: p28-text-0113
text: facilities in other respects. It was the only building

name: p28-text-0114
text: at the arsenal which had doors wide enough to permit

name: p28-text-0115
text: tracks entering one end of the craneway and its cranes

name: p28-text-0116
text: offered excellent facilities for moving material from

name: p28-text-0117
text: the cars to the floor and for transferring material

name: p28-text-0118
text: on the floor. Auto trucks could also unload inside the

name: p28-text-0119
text: building.

name: p28-text-0120
text: In addition to handling component parts, the cranes

name: p28-text-0121
text: were used for advancing the tanks along the floor

name: p28-text-0122
text: during the various stages of assembly. The lack of

name: p28-text-0123
text: space made it impossible to complete a tank in place;

name: p28-text-0124
text: it necessarily had to be handled on a progressive as-

name: p28-text-0125
text: sembly basis, very similar to that used at most auto-

name: p28-text-0126
text: mobile factories. Machine space adjoining the assem-

name: p28-text-0127
text: bly floor was used for the storage of component parts

name: p28-text-0128
text: and for a certain part of the sub-assembly work.

name: p28-text-0129
text: The road test followed the assembly, a suitable field

name: p28-text-0130
text: located at the southwest corner of the island, approxi-

name: p28-text-0131
text: mately three-quarters of a mile from the shops, being

name: p28-text-0132
text: utilized. Access to this ground was had by means of

name: p28-text-0133
text: two roads, one paved, the other unpaved. An inter-

name: p28-text-0134
text: esting fact developed was that to pay for the repair of

name: p28-text-0135
text: the paved road, due to use by tanks, was more eco-

name: p28-text-0136
text: nomical than to use the unpaved road and pay for

name: p28-text-0137
text: the cleaning of the tanks.

name: p28-text-0138
text: Additional Facilities Needed

name: p28-text-0139
text: In order to be able to carry on this work in the

name: p28-text-0140
text: craneway of Shop M, it was necessary to move all

name: p28-text-0141
text: salvaged machinery and material stored there. The

name: p28-text-0142
text: work of moving the machinery was delayed due to

name: p28-text-0143
text: the fact that other machinery, declared obsolete, had

name: p28-text-0144
text: to be moved before the salvaged machinery could be

name: p28-text-0145
text: handled.

name: p28-text-0146
text: Prior to the moving of the salvaged machinery and

name: p28-text-0147
text: material, there was only 6,500 square feet available

name: p28-text-0148
text: floor space in which to carry on the assembly of the

name: p28-text-0149
text: tanks. After all this had been cleared away, approxi-

name: p28-text-0150
text: mately 25,000 square feet of floor space was then

name: p28-text-0151
text: available.

name: p28-text-0152
text: As the work proceeded it developed that additional

name: p28-text-0153
text: floor space must be provided. This space was fur-

name: p28-text-0154
text: nished by taking over parts of the first and second

name: p28-text-0155
text: wing and a large portion of the bay of the first floor,

name: p28-text-0156
text: adding approximately 15,000 square feet, and giving

name: p28-text-0157
text: a total of 40,000 square feet.

name: p28-text-0158
text: The second wing of the first floor was used for the

name: p28-text-0159
text: repair and modification of Liberty motors and trans-

name: p28-text-0160
text: missions, requiring the installation of overhead trol-

name: p28-text-0161
text: leys.

name: p28-text-0162
text: In addition to this a number of the sub-assemblies

name: p28-text-0163
text: were made in different buildings, as there was no

name: p28-text-0164
text: available space for these in the craneway or in the

name: p28-text-0165
text: other parts of Shop M. The craneway not being de-

name: p28-text-0166
text: signed for assembly work, it became necessary to

name: p28-text-0167
text: install high pressure air lines for the air hammers and

name: p28-text-0168
text: wiring for the electric rivet heaters. Then, the elec-

name: p28-text-0169
text: tric rivet heaters not furnishing rivets as fast as they

name: p28-text-0170
text: were used by the various riveting gangs, it became

name: p28-text-0171
text: necessary to install crude-oil furnaces with incidental

name: p28-text-0172
text: low-pressure air piping.

name: p28-text-0173
text: Wood horses, trestles and benches were also needed

name: p28-text-0174
text: in large quantities for the large force of men engaged

name: p28-text-0175
text: in riveting.

name: p28-text-0176
text: Organization

name: p28-text-0177
text: A great deal of difficulty was encountered in build-

name: p28-text-0178
text: ing up an organization suitable for handling this class

name: p28-text-0179
text: of work, this being the first time work of this nature

name: p28-text-0180
text: had ever been attempted at this island.

name: p28-text-0181
text: During the assembly period; i. e., from September

name: p28-text-0182
text: 1, 1919, the time when the work really got under way,

name: p28-text-0183
text: to June 10, 1920, the date the last tank was completed,

name: p28-text-0184
text: the arsenal witnessed a very high percentage of labor

name: p28-text-0185
text: turnover on this particular job. During this time

name: p28-text-0186
text: there were approximately 3,000 employees engaged

name: p28-text-0187
text: upon this assembly work, although at no time were

name: p28-text-0188
text: there more than 819 employees actually on the floor;

name: p28-text-0189
text: in other words, the labor turnover in a period of ap-

name: p28-text-0190
text: proximately nine and one-half months was virtually

name: p28-text-0191
text: 400 per cent. It is to be noted that these figures per-

name: p28-text-0192
text: tain only to the assembly work and not to the per-

name: p28-text-0193
text: sonnel engaged upon the manufacture of component

name: p28-text-0194
text: parts. The difficulty of making satisfactory progress

name: p28-text-0195
text: under such adverse conditions can well be appreciated

name: p28-text-0196
text: by anyone familiar with manufacturing work. This

name: p28-text-0197
text: tremendous turnover was due to exceptionally high

name: p28-text-0198
text: wages paid on the outside (Government adjustments

name: p28-text-0199
text: of wages having to follow commercial firms and not

name: p28-text-0200
text: precede), and to the fact that knowing that the work

name: p28-text-0201
text: at the arsenal would practically cease on June 30,

name: p28-text-0202
text: 1920, men were seeking permanent employment else-

name: p28-text-0203
text: where.

name: p28-text-0204
text: Sub-Assemblies

name: p28-text-0205
text: In planning the work of assembling the Mark VIII

name: p28-text-0206
text: tanks, it was advisable to divide the work into various

name: p28-text-0207
text: Train load of thirty-four cars carrying Mark VIII Tanks

name: p29-text-0209
text: sub-assemblies, allowing the work to be placed on as

name: p29-text-0210
text: nearly a production basis as possible; i. e., keeping

name: p29-text-0211
text: a certain force of men on each separate, distinct

name: p29-text-0212
text: operation.

name: p29-text-0213
text: In the assembly of each Mark VIII tank there are

name: p29-text-0214
text: approximately 250 sub-assemblies; and, as previously

name: p29-text-0215
text: stated, due to the limited amount of floor space, it

name: p29-text-0216
text: was necessary to make some sub-assemblies in various

name: p29-text-0217
text: departments throughout the entire Artillery Vehicle

name: p29-text-0218
text: Section.

name: p29-text-0219
text: Among the most important of these sub-assemblies

name: p29-text-0220
text: were:

name: p29-text-0221
text: Side doors for main hull,

name: p29-text-0222
text: Petrol cover doors,

name: p29-text-0223
text: Ammunition chests,

name: p29-text-0224
text: Outside tool boxes,

name: p29-text-0225
text: Peep-hole covers,

name: p29-text-0226
text: Engine-room doors,

name: p29-text-0227
text: Switchboards,

name: p29-text-0228
text: Officers’ chests,

name: p29-text-0229
text: Ball mounts,

name: p29-text-0230
text: Tin-hat compartments,

name: p29-text-0231
text: Gauge boards,

name: p29-text-0232
text: Shell-stop bars,

name: p29-text-0233
text: Pressure-regulating tanks,

name: p29-text-0234
text: Combination tap bodies for petrol tanks.

name: p29-text-0235
text: The Liberty motor, when received at this arsenal,

name: p29-text-0236
text: was supposed to be ready for installation into the

name: p29-text-0237
text: tank, but it developed that, owing to this being an

name: p29-text-0238
text: airplane type motor, some modifications would be nec-

name: p29-text-0239
text: essary before the motor would be suitable for the

name: p29-text-0240
text: heavy duty to which it was to be subjected in the tank.

name: p29-text-0241
text: All were modified by changing from the Zenith to a

name: p29-text-0242
text: Ball & Ball carburetor, and by installing in each gov-

name: p29-text-0243
text: ernor a ball cup and retainer. It was also necessary

name: p29-text-0244
text: to remove the distributor heads to synchronize them

name: p29-text-0245
text: and to time the cylinders according to the breaker

name: p29-text-0246
text: box.

name: p29-text-0247
text: The transmission was not suitable for the tank until

name: p29-text-0248
text: some modifications had been made. The insertion of

name: p29-text-0249
text: a reinforced internal gear was no short nor simple job.

name: p29-text-0250
text: Order of Assembly

name: p29-text-0251
text: The main hull was the largest assembly and re-

name: p29-text-0252
text: quired a force of thirty rivet drivers, thirty buckers

name: p29-text-0253
text: and thirty heaters to keep this assembly moving fast

name: p29-text-0254
text: enough for the men making the sub-assemblies into the

name: p29-text-0255
text: main hull. This work consisted of the assembly of

name: p29-text-0256
text: such parts as the girders, hull, side plates, mud chutes,

name: p29-text-0257
text: roofs, floors, turrets and road track rollers. The

name: p29-text-0258
text: majority of the material mentioned above is ½-inch

name: p29-text-0259
text: armor plate and angle iron, secured together by ap-

name: p29-text-0260
text: proximately 8,000 11-16 inch rivets—a job of riveting

name: p29-text-0261
text: requiring great care in many cases. The man and

name: p29-text-0262
text: officer’s turrets are the second largest sub-assemblies

name: p29-text-0263
text: on the tank.

name: p29-text-0264
text: Engine Room Assembly

name: p29-text-0265
text: The placing of the transmission follows the hull

name: p29-text-0266
text: assembly. The motor then follows, connecting to the

name: p29-text-0267
text: transmission by means of compound clutch (epicyclic

name: p29-text-0268
text: type).

name: p29-text-0269
text: The cooling system, consisting of radiator, water

name: p29-text-0270
text: tank, sirocco fan and fan drive, is next installed.

name: p29-text-0271
text: The electrical equipment follows, consisting of:

name: p29-text-0272
text: One 12-volt generator, used for ignition,

name: p29-text-0273
text: Two 6-volt generators, used for lights, batteries

name: p29-text-0274
text: and spark,

name: p29-text-0275
text: Two 12-volt storage batteries,

name: p29-text-0276
text: One 6-volt storage battery.

name: p29-text-0277
text: At this time all wiring necessary for the lighting,

name: p29-text-0278
text: ignition and control is put in place. These wires are

name: p29-text-0279
text: all run through flexible conduit for protection from

name: p29-text-0280
text: fire and damage by walking on them or by coming in

name: p29-text-0281
text: contact with metal parts about the motor and trans-

name: p29-text-0282
text: mission.

name: p29-text-0283
text: The petrol and air pressure systems are then in-

name: p29-text-0284
text: stalled. The petrol system, consisting of three 50-

name: p29-text-0285
text: gallon petrol tanks, is located in the rear of the tank,

name: p29-text-0286
text: back of the engine room, and is protected from the

name: p29-text-0287
text: sides of the tank by means of wood packing strips

name: p29-text-0288
text: covered with felt. The flow of gasoline is regulated

name: p29-text-0289
text: through a pressure-regulating tank located just over

name: p29-text-0290
text: the motor. This practically completes the engine-

name: p29-text-0291
text: room sub-assemblies.

name: p29-text-0292
text: Fighting-Compartment Assembly

name: p29-text-0293
text: The remaining sub-assemblies are then confined to

name: p29-text-0294
text: the fighting compartment, which consists in the as-

name: p29-text-0295
text: sembling of the gun-hanger bracket for Browning

name: p29-text-0296
text: machine guns, ball mounts, periscope and spare barrel

name: p29-text-0297
text: clips, peep-hole covers, head rests, periscope holders,

name: p29-text-0298
text: semaphores, fire extinguishers, brackets, control units,

name: p29-text-0299
text: driver’s seat, engine-room doors, tin-hat compart-

name: p29-text-0300
text: ments, officers’ chest and various other miscellaneous

name: p29-text-0301
text: assemblies.

name: p29-text-0302
text: While the assembly of the sponsons is one of the

name: p29-text-0303
text: largest sub-assemblies and one of the first started, the

name: p29-text-0304
text: sponsons are not assembled to the tanks until prac-

name: p29-text-0305
text: tically the very last. The sponson itself consists of

name: p29-text-0306
text: armor plate, angle iron, ammunition storage chests,

name: p29-text-0307
text: from Rock Island Arsenal, Ill., to Camp Meade, Md., May 21, 1920

name: p30-text-0308
text: ARMY ORDNANCE

name: p30-text-0310
text: Hotchkiss 6-pounder guns, sponson track rollers and

name: p30-text-0311
text: gunners’ seat.

name: p30-text-0312
text: Caterpillar Assembly

name: p30-text-0313
text: The driving sprockets are placed on the tank, fol-

name: p30-text-0314
text: lowed by the track shoes, consisting of two tracks of

name: p30-text-0315
text: 78 shoes each. The tracks are assembled to the hull

name: p30-text-0316
text: as follows: Four sections comprise the complete as-

name: p30-text-0317
text: sembly; two sections are laid upon the floor, the

name: p30-text-0318
text: proper length of the hull. The hull is then raised

name: p30-text-0319
text: and set upon these sections. A crane cable is then

name: p30-text-0320
text: hooked to one end of another section and raised high

name: p30-text-0321
text: enough so that the link can be coupled to the section

name: p30-text-0322
text: which is on the floor. It is then drawn along the top

name: p30-text-0323
text: of the tank, at the same time lowering the track to the

name: p30-text-0324
text: hull. The tracks having been adjusted to proper ten-

name: p30-text-0325
text: sion on the hull by the track-adjusting screws, the

name: p30-text-0326
text: tank is ready for road test.

name: p30-text-0327
text: Product of Components

name: p30-text-0328
text: Most of the component parts that were to be used

name: p30-text-0329
text: in the construction of the Mark VIII tank were pur-

name: p30-text-0330
text: chased by this country from the British Government.

name: p30-text-0331
text: These parts consisted of the heavy structural parts

name: p30-text-0332
text: of the tank, i. e., armor plate, angle iron, steel girders

name: p30-text-0333
text: and channels, and a large quantity of the equipment

name: p30-text-0334
text: carried, such as tools, Hotchkiss guns, camouflage

name: p30-text-0335
text: nets, water cans, bird cages, food cans, telescopes,

name: p30-text-0336
text: periscopes, festoon lamps, semaphores and various

name: p30-text-0337
text: other sundries. All material shipped from England

name: p30-text-0338
text: to this country was sent to Raritan Arsenal for tempo-

name: p30-text-0339
text: rary storage, for reshipment to Rock Island Arsenal.

name: p30-text-0340
text: The balance of the material required in construction

name: p30-text-0341
text: was manufactured by various outside contractors

name: p30-text-0342
text: throughout the United States and was also shipped to

name: p30-text-0343
text: Raritan Arsenal. These items were the Liberty mo-

name: p30-text-0344
text: tors, transmissions, compound clutches, petrol tanks,

name: p30-text-0345
text: radiators, electrical equipment and front control

name: p30-text-0346
text: units.

name: p30-text-0347
text: Upon the first inventory of material received it

name: p30-text-0348
text: was found that only 65 per cent of the necessary mate-

name: p30-text-0349
text: rial was on hand, and Raritan Arsenal reported that

name: p30-text-0350
text: many of the essential parts needed had not been re-

name: p30-text-0351
text: ceived at that arsenal from the contractors. It then

name: p30-text-0352
text: became necessary to send men to a number of these

name: p30-text-0353
text: contractors throughout this country to urge comple-

name: p30-text-0354
text: tion of the work, to trace and have the shipment of

name: p30-text-0355
text: these parts expedited. Due to congested freight con-

name: p30-text-0356
text: ditions, strikes and other causes it was impossible to

name: p30-text-0357
text: Rock Island ruggedness of construction was strikingly demonstrated when this overturned tank, on being righted, started off under its own power

name: p31-text-0358
text: MARK VIII TANKS

name: p31-text-0360
text: procure some of these parts in time to be of any

name: p31-text-0361
text: assistance in the assembly and, therefore, a number

name: p31-text-0362
text: of parts were manufactured here to prevent delay in

name: p31-text-0363
text: production.

name: p31-text-0364
text: It was necessary to purchase bolts, rivets, lock

name: p31-text-0365
text: washers, pipe fittings, angle iron, gauges, tubing, raw

name: p31-text-0366
text: material and numerous other items in large quantities.

name: p31-text-0367
text: The rivets used in most of the assemblies were an odd

name: p31-text-0368
text: size, not in common use in this country, and it was a

name: p31-text-0369
text: difficult matter to secure proper stock for manu-

name: p31-text-0370
text: facture.

name: p31-text-0371
text: Manufacture of Components

name: p31-text-0372
text: As stated above, approximately 35 per cent of the

name: p31-text-0373
text: parts entering into the construction of the Mark VIII

name: p31-text-0374
text: tanks had to be manufactured at this arsenal. These

name: p31-text-0375
text: consisted of such parts as outside tool boxes, unditch-

name: p31-text-0376
text: ing angles, roller sprockets, roof, side, front and rear

name: p31-text-0377
text: towing brackets; sponson hinges on hull, engine-con-

name: p31-text-0378
text: trol rods, battery shelf assembly, shell tubes, combi-

name: p31-text-0379
text: nation tap bodies, petrol-tank packing, track adjust-

name: p31-text-0380
text: ing screws, bolts, nuts, cap screws and pins.

name: p31-text-0381
text: In the manufacture of these items it was necessary

name: p31-text-0382
text: to make special tools, jigs and fixtures in order to get

name: p31-text-0383
text: production. It might be well to state, however, that

name: p31-text-0384
text: most of the parts which were manufactured at this

name: p31-text-0385
text: arsenal for the first 25 tanks were made without the

name: p31-text-0386
text: assistance of any special tools, jigs or fixtures of any

name: p31-text-0387
text: kind, in order to avoid delay in production; and in

name: p31-text-0388
text: this way it gave a better idea as to just what tool,

name: p31-text-0389
text: jig, or fixture would be best adapted for the work.

name: p31-text-0390
text: This also gave time to have these tools, jigs and fix-

name: p31-text-0391
text: tures manufactured so that they could be used in the

name: p31-text-0392
text: balance of the material required.

name: p31-text-0393
text: The items of bolts, nuts, cap screws and pins, as

name: p31-text-0394
text: listed above, was probably one of the largest items

name: p31-text-0395
text: which had to be contended with, as this quantity ran

name: p31-text-0396
text: into the hundreds of thousands. The manufacture

name: p31-text-0397
text: of bolts for this job alone kept approximately 25

name: p31-text-0398
text: mechanics and 30 turret lathes and automatic screw

name: p31-text-0399
text: machines busy for a period of about four months. To

name: p31-text-0400
text: better explain the quantity required, there was one

name: p31-text-0401
text: item of ⅝-inch tap bolts, Whitworth thread, of which

name: p31-text-0402
text: there were 20,000 required for the manufacture of

name: p31-text-0403
text: these Mark VIII tanks.

name: p31-text-0404
text: A quantity of the armor plate was received without

name: p31-text-0405
text: heat treatment, and it was necessary that this armor

name: p31-text-0406
text: plate be heat-treated before it could be used in the

name: p31-text-0407
text: assembly of tanks. As this was practically the first

name: p31-text-0408
text: time any work of this nature had been attempted at

name: p31-text-0409
text: this arsenal, it was necessary to do a certain amount

name: p31-text-0410
text: of experimenting to produce satisfactory results.

name: p31-text-0411
text: Practically all of the armor plate, steel angle iron,

name: p31-text-0412
text: steel girders, etc., received at this arsenal had to be

name: p31-text-0413
text: straightened to conform to drawings. This required

name: p31-text-0414
text: a force of approximately 50 sheet-metal straighteners

name: p31-text-0415
text: and helpers. These men were employed continually

name: p31-text-0416
text: on this work during the entire period of construction.

name: p31-text-0417
text: As much of this material was manufactured from

name: p31-text-0418
text: castings, it was necessary to keep a force of pattern-

name: p31-text-0419
text: makers and molders continuously on this work.

name: p31-text-0420
text: There was a large amount of wood work necessary

name: p31-text-0421
text: for these tanks, such as packing for petrol tanks,

name: p31-text-0422
text: switchboards, gauge boards, shell-tube boards, map

name: p31-text-0423
text: boards, Browning machine-gun rest blocks and offi-

name: p31-text-0424
text: cers’ chests.

name: p31-text-0425
text: Tests

name: p31-text-0426
text: On February 2, 1919, a sample Mark VIII tank was

name: p31-text-0427
text: received at Rock Island Arsenal from Bridgeport,

name: p31-text-0428
text: Conn. After remaining at this arsenal for a few

name: p31-text-0429
text: days it was ordered out for exhibition purposes to

name: p31-text-0430
text: Clinton, Iowa; Iowa City, Iowa; Ottawa Beach,

name: p31-text-0431
text: Mich., and Denver, Colo. It was then returned and

name: p31-text-0432
text: sent to Savanna Proving Ground, Ill., where it re-

name: p31-text-0433
text: ceived a road test of 2,155 miles.

name: p31-text-0434
text: A force of men familiar with the handling and op-

name: p31-text-0435
text: erating of the Mark VIII tank were transferred from

name: p31-text-0436
text: the Rock Island Arsenal to Savanna Proving Ground

name: p31-text-0437
text: to handle this road test, which was conducted to de-

name: p31-text-0438
text: termine any defects in the design of the working parts

name: p32-text-0439
text: ARMY ORDNANCE

name: p32-text-0441
text: of this tank. The most serious trouble developed by

name: p32-text-0442
text: this test was the stripping of the teeth in the sprocket

name: p32-text-0443
text: roller pinions. It also developed that the exhaust

name: p32-text-0444
text: system designed and in use on this tank was not suit-

name: p32-text-0445
text: able; that the Zenith carburetor originally designed

name: p32-text-0446
text: for the 12-cylinder Liberty motor of the aeroplane

name: p32-text-0447
text: design was not suitable for this class of work and

name: p32-text-0448
text: would have to be replaced with a Ball & Ball car-

name: p32-text-0449
text: buretor; that the V-belt driving the sirocco was un-

name: p32-text-0450
text: satisfactory, calling for a replacement with a 3-inch

name: p32-text-0451
text: leather belt, necessitating the changing of the V-pul-

name: p32-text-0452
text: leys to cast-iron flanged pulleys.

name: p32-text-0453
text: The design and material used in the petrol tank

name: p32-text-0454
text: caused considerable trouble due to rust and scale

name: p32-text-0455
text: getting into the carburetor. This caused some back-

name: p32-text-0456
text: firing through the carburetor; and in a number of

name: p32-text-0457
text: instances fires occurred, damaging the electrical

name: p32-text-0458
text: equipment.

name: p32-text-0459
text: This road test was given only to the original tank

name: p32-text-0460
text: shipped from Bridgeport; but each tank was given a

name: p32-text-0461
text: four-hours’ shop test to determine the satisfactory

name: p32-text-0462
text: operation of the motor and to make any necessary ad-

name: p32-text-0463
text: justments. Upon the completion of this shop test, the

name: p32-text-0464
text: tank was then placed on a road test for ten hours;

name: p32-text-0465
text: after the road test it was carefully gone over and in-

name: p32-text-0466
text: spected, cleaned, painted and prepared for shipment.

name: p32-text-0467
text: Difficulties Encountered

name: p32-text-0468
text: In addition to difficulties mentioned under the

name: p32-text-0469
text: heading of tests, the following are a few of the more

name: p32-text-0470
text: serious difficulties encountered:

name: p32-text-0471
text: (a) On practically all the material which had to be

name: p32-text-0472
text: riveted together it was necessary to drift the holes,

name: p32-text-0473
text: due to inaccurate drilling, or to the expansion or con-

name: p32-text-0474
text: traction of these plates during the process of heat-

name: p32-text-0475
text: treating. It became necessary in many cases to weld

name: p32-text-0476
text: these holes and to redrill.

name: p32-text-0477
text: (b) In many instances cracks appeared in the ar-

name: p32-text-0478
text: mor after the plates were riveted in place. It was

name: p32-text-0479
text: then necessary to remove these plates, necessitating

name: p32-text-0480
text: the cutting out of all rivets. These cracks were so

name: p32-text-0481
text: slight that they could not be detected before assem-

name: p32-text-0482
text: bly and only appeared due to impact of the riveting

name: p32-text-0483
text: hammers.

name: p32-text-0484
text: (c) When attempt was made to assemble the

name: p32-text-0485
text: Hotchkiss guns to the sponsons, the base was found

name: p32-text-0486
text: to be out of true, and it was necessary to remove them

name: p32-text-0487
text: from the mounts and straighten them in hydraulic

name: p32-text-0488
text: presses.

name: p32-text-0489
text: (d) Due to faulty design and construction of the

name: p32-text-0490
text: petrol tanks, leaks were often discovered after assem-

name: p32-text-0491
text: bly, and much trouble and delay was encountered in

name: p32-text-0492
text: attempting to keep up the necessary pressure required

name: p32-text-0493
text: to send gasoline to the carburetor.

name: p32-text-0494
text: (e) The revolving peep-hole plates, made of armor

name: p32-text-0495
text: plate and about 6 inches in diameter, when received

name: p32-text-0496
text: were so warped that they had to be surface ground

name: p32-text-0497
text: on both sides before they could be used. There were

name: p32-text-0498
text: 22 of these required for each tank, making a total

name: p32-text-0500
text: Incidents of Construction

name: p32-text-0501
text: The construction of the first Mark VIII tank was

name: p32-text-0502
text: started July 1, 1919, and the last tank was completed

name: p32-text-0503
text: and ready for road test on June 5, 1920, making a

name: p32-text-0504
text: total of 286 days to complete the 100 tanks. The first

name: p32-text-0505
text: tank was completed on January 5, 1920, and the last

name: p32-text-0506
text: just five months later, making a total of 150 days

name: p32-text-0507
text: used in the assembly of the tanks after getting on a

name: p32-text-0508
text: production basis, or on the average of one tank every

name: p32-text-0509
text: 36 hours on the basis of working 24 hours per day.

name: p32-text-0510
text: The general assembly on the tanks did not start until

name: p32-text-0511
text: about September 1, 1919, due to the fact that a great

name: p32-text-0512
text: deal of time was spent in checking in material and

name: p32-text-0513
text: waiting for the receipt of the various component parts

name: p32-text-0514
text: which were to be shipped to this arsenal by Raritan

name: p32-text-0515
text: Arsenal.

name: p32-text-0516
text: The greatest number of tanks which were produced

name: p32-text-0517
text: in one week of six days was seven. The greatest num-

name: p32-text-0518
text: ber of tanks under construction at any one time was

name: p32-text-0519
text: twenty-eight.

name: p32-text-0520
text: On November 13, 1919, the Tank Section was di-

name: p32-text-0521
text: vided into three 8-hour shifts; 50 per cent of the men

name: p32-text-0522
text: being employed on day shift, 30 per cent on the first

name: p32-text-0523
text: night shift and 20 per cent on the second night shift.

name: p32-text-0524
text: The only “near” serious accident during the con-

name: p32-text-0525
text: struction of the tanks occurred on March 22, 1920,

name: p32-text-0526
text: while loading one of the tanks for shipment. The

name: p32-text-0527
text: sill of the flat car gave way, allowing the tank to turn

name: p32-text-0528
text: turtle off the car. The only damage resulting from

name: p32-text-0529
text: this accident was a slight dent in the roof of the

name: p32-text-0530
text: main turret and the bending of the semaphone, which

name: p32-text-0531
text: damages were very easily repaired without removing

name: p32-text-0532
text: the parts from the tank. The driver and mechanic,

name: p32-text-0533
text: who were in the tank at the time, were in no way

name: p32-text-0534
text: injured other than being slightly shaken up. The

name: p32-text-0535
text: tank was righted by coupling another tank to it with

name: p32-text-0536
text: towing cables and rolling it completely back on its

name: p32-text-0537
text: track, after which it proceeded to the shop on its

name: p32-text-0538
text: own power for necessary repairs.

name: p32-text-0539
text: On March 29, 1920, during road test of a tank at

name: p32-text-0540
text: the testing ground, near the west end of the island,

name: p32-text-0541
text: one of the tanks was run too close to the water’s edge

name: p32-text-0542
text: and in some manner slipped off, burying itself in the

name: p32-text-0543
text: mud and water. The river stage was unusually high

name: p32-text-0544
text: at this time of the year, and water coming in contact

name: p32-text-0545
text: with the ignition system made it impossible to get the

name: p32-text-0546
text: tank out with its own power. It was towed from the

name: p32-text-0547
text: river by coupling two Mark VIII tanks together.

name: p32-text-0548
text: While under road test a number of tanks caught

name: p32-text-0549
text: fire, through back-firing through the carburetor.

name: p32-text-0550
text: These fires caused very slight damages and were easily

name: p33-text-0551
text: MARK VIII TANKS

name: p33-text-0553
text: extinguished by the use of fire extinguishers supplied

name: p33-text-0554
text: to the tanks for any emergency of this nature. There

name: p33-text-0555
text: was no one at any time injured or seriously burned in

name: p33-text-0556
text: any fires of this nature.

name: p33-text-0557
text: The greatest number of men employed at any one

name: p33-text-0558
text: time in the Tank Section was 819. Of this number

name: p33-text-0559
text: there was approximately 10 per cent absent each

name: p33-text-0560
text: working day. Due to the large labor turnover of em-

name: p33-text-0561
text: ployees in this section, a great deal of time was ex-

name: p33-text-0562
text: pended in instructing these men in the various opera-

name: p33-text-0563
text: tions entering into the construction of the Mark

name: p33-text-0564
text: VIII tanks.

name: p33-text-0565
text: The following are averages of the different classes

name: p33-text-0566
text: of labor used in the construction:

name: p33-text-0567
text: 15 foremen and assistant foremen,

name: p33-text-0568
text: 25 sheet-metal straighteners,

name: p33-text-0569
text: 45 machinists,

name: p33-text-0570
text: 30 heaters,

name: p33-text-0571
text: 65 specialists,

name: p33-text-0572
text: 100 assemblers,

name: p33-text-0573
text: 30 riveters,

name: p33-text-0574
text: 300 skilled laborers,

name: p33-text-0575
text: 30 buckers,

name: p33-text-0576
text: 200 laborers,

name: p33-text-0577
text: 8 clerks in the office personnel, which included sten-

name: p33-text-0578
text: ographer, follow-up men and messengers.

name: p33-text-0579
text: The successful completion of the job on schedule

name: p33-text-0580
text: time was due to the exceptional interest in the work

name: p33-text-0581
text: and the loyalty and co-operation of the foremen and

name: p33-text-0582
text: permanent workers on the job.

name: p33-text-0583
text: The completion of these tanks was promised the

name: p33-text-0584
text: Chief of Ordnance by June 15, 1920. It gave the

name: p33-text-0585
text: writer great pleasure to inform General Williams of

name: p33-text-0586
text: the completion of the last tank on June 10, 1920.
